issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 3 (b). Blocked by Phase 3a.

## Task
- `rules.yaml` shipped in the leaf and read from ~/.config/org-rule-guard/rules.yaml (XDG honoured):
  one entry per rule with id, tools, patterns (regex), path globs where relevant, message, enabled.
  Python keeps only the engine (input parsing, matching, deny output, logging).
- The credential rule becomes a delegation to `agent-secrets/hooks/credential-guard.py` (import or
  subprocess), so the two guards no longer carry duplicate pattern lists.
- A malformed rules file fails open with one logged `rules_load_error` line, matching the hook contract.

## Acceptance
- The six default rules produce the same allow/deny decisions as Phase 3a on the same fixtures.
- Adding a rule in YAML (no Python change) blocks a new fixture; disabling one allows it.
- Documented so a promoted lesson (NEEDLE ADR-027) can land as a YAML entry under review.
issue.title: org-rule-guard: move rules to ~/.config/org-rule-guard/rules.yaml and delegate the credential rule to credential-guard (Phase 3b)

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 3 (a). Companion to NEEDLE plan section 4.4 (operator-side loop).

## Why
The org-wide PreToolUse guard at ~/.claude/hooks/org-rule-guard.py (332 lines, six rules) has exactly
one output path: the deny JSON on stdout. Nothing records which rule fired, in which repo, how often.
The enforcement layer emits no learning signal, so CLAUDE.md prose cannot be tuned against evidence.

## Task
1. Create utilities/org-rule-guard/ as a leaf: hooks/org-rule-guard.py (ported from the live hook,
   same six rules, same fail-open contract), hooks/test_org_rule_guard.py (one allow and one deny
   fixture per rule, built at runtime so no rule-triggering literal sits in the test file), install.sh
   (idempotent copy into ~/.claude/hooks/; edits settings.json only with --wire), README.md, VERSION.
2. On every deny, append one JSON line to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/org-rule-guard/denials.jsonl:
   ts (UTC ISO-8601), rule_id (stable slug), tool, cwd, session_id (from the hook input if present), and
   a redacted 80-char fragment of what matched. For the credential rule the fragment is the pattern
   name only; never a value. Directory mode 700. Logging failures never change the decision.
3. README: log format plus a jq recipe for "denials by rule_id, last 7 days".

## Acceptance
- Test suite passes against both the live hook and the ported copy on the same fixtures.
- A deny writes exactly one line; an allow writes nothing.
- install.sh without --wire does not touch ~/.claude/settings.json or overwrite an existing hook file.
issue.notes: Duplicate dispatch: a prior session on this bead shipped and pushed 09c4841 + a878e20 at 09:21-09:23 while this session was independently verifying the same work; its tree is byte-identical to what it committed, so nothing was rebuilt. This session verified the shipped state instead of duplicating it: 35 tests green against the ported copy and 35 run/15 log tests skipped green against ~/.claude/hooks/org-rule-guard.py on the same fixtures (ORG_RULE_GUARD_UNDER_TEST); a deny appends exactly one JSONL line (ts/rule_id/tool/cwd/session_id/fragment) and an allow appends nothing and stays silent at exit 0; state dir 700 and file 600 via a single O_APPEND write; the credential rule logs its pattern name only and a runtime-built fake ghp_ token appears nowhere in the log, including on a mixed command where the credential rule wins ordering; bare install.sh against the real HOME left the live hook sha256-identical and ~/.claude/settings.json untouched; the README jq recipe was checked against a synthetic log holding 1/3/10/20-day-old records and correctly counts only the 7-day window; and a live-vs-ported comparison over 8 allow/deny cases matched on every decision with byte-equal deny reasons. Also fixed the stale plan Components section (9233117, pushed) which still described the hook as planned and reading rules from a rules.yaml that is 3(b), and tagged org-rule-guard/v0.1.0 at 09c4841 per the documented per-utility tag convention.

issue.description:
plan.md specifies a detailed behavioral contract for org-rule-guard's install.sh — idempotent copy into ~/.claude/hooks/, never overwriting a hook already at the destination, never touching settings.json without an explicit `--wire`, and `--uninstall` refusing a file this folder did not install — but no test file covers any of it (test_org_rule_guard.py exercises the hook, not the installer). Add unittest coverage that drives install.sh inside a temp HOME for each contract clause, including the refusal paths, and include this suite in the Phase 2 Argo CI run so the contract stays enforced.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes: Verified complete as shipped by the two prior attempts; nothing further to commit. Coverage (commit 25a3570, Install class in org-rule-guard/hooks/test_org_rule_guard.py, 15 tests): temp-$HOME default destinations; first install copies hook and leaves settings.json absent; no-overwrite without --force/--wire; --force overwrites but still leaves settings alone; --wire writes and idempotently merges (preserves unrelated keys and a pre-existing PreToolUse entry); --wire replaces an existing copy; --uninstall removes the hook, leaves settings and the denial log untouched, and REFUSES (exit 1, 'refusing' on stderr, file survives) a destination file this folder did not install, with --force as the override. Verified live: python3 -m unittest discover -s org-rule-guard/hooks -v -> 38 tests OK locally; Argo run utilities-ci-pbp64 (iad-ci) Succeeded on revision c8c7ba5 (HEAD, contains 25a3570) with the suite at utilities-ci-workflowtemplate.yml line 172 plus shellcheck on install.sh. plan.md already documents both the suite and Phase 2 as shipped.

issue.description:
Both hooks have documented unittest suites (test_credential_guard.py, test_org_rule_guard.py), but `bin/bao-as` — the AppRole login wrapper whose whole job is keeping secret-store tokens out of argv — has no test mentioned anywhere in plan.md. Add a unittest suite that, using a stub `bao` binary on PATH and a temp BAO config dir, verifies: credentials reach the login only via `@file` (never as argv literals), the token is exported only into the child's environment and never printed, `exec` passthrough preserves exit code and stdio, and missing or world-readable credential files fail closed. Fixtures must be built at runtime so no credential-shaped literal sits in the test file, matching the convention of the two existing suites.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes: Shipped agent-secrets/bin/test_bao_as.py (19 tests) + commit 24ba441. Suite runs the wrapper against a stub `bao` first on PATH and a throwaway BAO_AS_CONFIG_DIR, per the four required contracts: (1) login argv is exactly write/-field=token/auth/approle/login/role_id=@/secret_id=@ and the stub's own resolution of the @files yields the credential values, proving they travel as files; (2) the issued token lands only in the child's env (BAO_/VAULT_TOKEN+ADDR), never on stdout/stderr, overrides a stale inherited BAO_TOKEN/VAULT_TOKEN, and leaves temp HOME empty (no ~/.vault-token); (3) exec preserves exit code 42, stdout/stderr and stdin; (4) missing role_id/secret_id, world-readable (0644), group-readable (0640), unknown instance, missing table and failed login all fail closed (78/77/2) with the stub CLI never invoked. bao-as gained the enforcement the header promised but never implemented: a find -perm /0044 check refusing group/other-readable credentials (the bead's 'world-readable fails closed' clause was unverifiable without it). All fixtures runtime-built; no credential-shaped literal in the test file. Both existing suites still green (21 + 38). One finding worth keeping: ~/.local/bin/bao-as on this box is NOT an installed copy of the repo script -- it is an older fleet-specific variant (hard-coded openbao-v2/rs-manager/ardenone-manager, ex44 AppRole, ~/.config/openbao/ layout, no VAULT_* exports, no instance table) that the fleet's CLAUDE.md workflows depend on. BAO_AS_UNDER_TEST is documented as proving copies of THIS script, not any wrapper that happens to share the name; the docstring calls that trap out explicitly. Do not run agent-secrets/install.sh on codinghome -- it would overwrite the fleet variant.
